freshness_notes.bgs_geosure_current_products: July 2026 refreshes; several v8 datasets updated 16-23 July 2026

batches.c: INSPIRE polygons show indicative extent/position of registered freehold property. Exact polygon-to-candidate intersection and INSPIRE ID are required; the polygon is not a surveyed or legally definitive boundary.
Current INSPIRE files are republished monthly. Candidate evidence must preserve the publication month and polygon version; an older polygon must not be silently treated as current.

batches.t: INSPIRE ID to title-record relationship gate
batches.c: An INSPIRE ID can be used to relate an indicative polygon to title information, but title registration/plan evidence remains a separate record and must be matched exactly before ownership conclusions.

The chargeable National Polygon Service covers freehold and leasehold title polygons and richer identifiers. Open INSPIRE coverage is a subset, so missing open data is not proof of unregistered/no-title land.

Index polygons are mapped for title indexing and show indicative extent. Candidate geometry must not be promoted as a legal boundary or precise surveyed ownership line without title-plan/legal evidence.

batches.t: National Local Land Charges register gate
batches.c: Local land charges can restrict land use and bind successors. Candidate use requires an exact charge spatial extent/record; authority-level migration status alone is not a property charge.
HM Land Registry LLC spatial downloads cover migrated authorities and expand over time. Absence from the national download where an authority is not migrated is a coverage gap, not a negative result.
Enfield states its LLC1 register has moved to the National Digital Register. An Enfield candidate still requires an exact national-register search/charge match before any constraint is promoted.

Havering states it is in the initial stages of HM Land Registry migration and still maintains its statutory local register. National LLC absence cannot be used as a no-charge result for the Havering candidate.
Lambeth states its Local Land Charges Register has migrated to HM Land Registry while the council continues CON29 replies. Exact LLC and any complementary CON29 evidence must remain separate.
LLC results and CON29 enquiries cover different information. A clean LLC result cannot prove absence of road schemes, notices or other matters available through CON29 or separate searches.

batches.t: Coal Development High Risk Area gate
batches.c: The Development High Risk Area combines recorded shallow/surface coal-mining hazards. Exact intersection is required and, where applicable, a Coal Mining Risk Assessment supports development safety.

batches.t: Coal Development Low Risk / residual-hazard guard
batches.c: Low Risk Area status removes the usual statutory CMRA requirement but does not prove absence of unrecorded mining hazards. Negative scoring must remain fail-closed.
Mine-entry records contain known shafts/adits but the authority warns that unrecorded entries may exist. Exact point/zone-of-influence evidence is required; dataset absence is not proof of no hazard.

Mine plans can show historical workings and entries but require interpretation, scale/georeferencing and current site relationship. A plan covering an area is not itself parcel-level hazard confirmation.

Mining licence areas indicate licensed activity geography and must be read with related licence/open-cast records. A licence polygon does not by itself prove current workings or candidate instability.
For relevant development in a High Risk Area, the planning workflow may require specialist assessment and consultation. Candidate status requires exact risk-area and proposal-type evidence.
GeoSure combines six susceptibility processes at mapping scale. It is screening/planning evidence; site-specific geotechnical investigation is still required for foundation or viability conclusions.
Shrink-swell mapping indicates geological susceptibility, not observed movement at the candidate. Exact mapped class, foundation design, vegetation, drainage and site investigation are needed.
Slope-instability susceptibility depends on geology, gradient, water and human modification. A regional or 5km class cannot establish parcel stability without exact terrain/site evidence.

Soluble-rock susceptibility indicates potential dissolution/cavity formation. Candidate conclusions require exact geology and investigation; generalised grid classifications can over- or under-estimate local hazard.
Compressible deposits may settle under loading or groundwater change. The mapped susceptibility is not a bearing-capacity result and requires exact ground profile and geotechnical assessment.
Collapsible deposits can subside when loaded and wetted. Candidate impact requires exact deposit presence, groundwater/loading scenario and investigation.
Running-sand susceptibility concerns saturated sands/silts under flowing water. Exact geology, groundwater and excavation/dewatering method are required before construction-risk promotion.
The London and Thames Valley 3D product adds depth-dependent shrink-swell susceptibility. It still remains a regional hazard model and not a substitute for candidate boreholes or foundation design.
The UKHSA-BGS definitive dataset estimates probability that a property is above the Action Level. Exact address/site lookup is required; the free 1km indicative map is not definitive parcel evidence.
The Indicative Atlas assigns each 1km square the highest potential found within it. It is intentionally conservative/generalised and must not be converted directly into a candidate property result.

UKradon address search gives an estimated probability, not a measured radon level, and directs redevelopment sites toward more detailed geoscience advice. Measurement is required to know actual indoor level.
UKHSA guidance treats below-ground occupied spaces as increased risk regardless of general map status. A low mapped area cannot be used as a no-radon conclusion for basement development.

Environment Agency historic landfill data identifies known closed/historic sites but older information may be incomplete. Exact polygon/attribute match is required; absence is not proof of no former waste deposition.

Authorised landfill polygons represent sites currently authorised under environmental permitting. Exact candidate boundary/proximity and permit status are required before any land-use impact is promoted.
Public Registers Online contains environmental permits/licences and available compliance records. Candidate conclusions require exact permit/site/address matching and current status.

Pollution Inventory reports annual releases from large regulated industrial sites. It is facility-level emissions evidence, not a parcel contamination result; exact source/pathway/receptor assessment is required.
HSE is statutory consultee around major hazard sites and major accident hazard pipelines. Exact consultation-zone position and development type/scale are required before applying HSE advice.
Hazardous substances consent can create inner/middle/outer risk zones used for future planning consultation. Exact consent/site and zone intersection must be confirmed.

batches.t: HSE Planning Advice Web App development-sensitivity gate
batches.c: HSE advice depends on consultation-zone proximity plus development type, size and intensity. Proximity alone does not determine advise-against/not-advise-against outcome.
